title: Ansarallah threatens to strike Aramco; Elon Musk pours $276 million into midterms; Russia violated Trump’s “energy ceasefire,” Zelenskyy says
author: Drop Site News
content:

**Tuesday, October 13, 2026 -**_****_

_**Yemen** : Saudi-led coalition threatens Sana'a oil site strikes; Ansarallah
warns it will hit Aramco in retaliation. Riyadh airport still closed after
Ansarallah attacks. Iran offers to mediate Saudi-Ansarallah talks. Israeli
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is reportedly seeking Saudi approval to join
war against Ansarallah; Riyadh opposes move._

_**Palestine** : Israeli forces storm medical complex in Ramallah, raid
prominent rights groups. Israeli strike kills Palestinian in Gaza City as
four-year-old dies of earlier injuries. Israeli forces and settlers attack
olive harvesters across the occupied West Bank. Israel demolishes Palestinian
homes inside of Israel a day after displacing 300 residents. Netanyahu orders
prosecution of soldiers interviewed in NAZA._

_**Iran** : U.S. President Donald Trump dismisses reports of Chinese and
Russian assistance to Iran. International Monetary Fund forecasts economic
contraction in Middle East and Central Asia. UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham
blames Iran for alleged plot targeting U.S.-used airbase. Attacks on ships
near Strait of Hormuz reach highest intensity since war began._

_**Lebanon:** Israeli warplanes launch airstrikes across southern Lebanon
despite ceasefire. EU to establish mission to train Lebanese military and
security forces. 13-year-old killed, 24 wounded by unexploded munition._

_**U.S.** : Texas Republican Senate nominee Ken Paxton celebrated New Year's
in Dubai with two indicted fugitives. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani
orders first NYPD use-of-force review in a decade. Federal agents raid Ilhan
Omar's D.C. home in immigration probe. ICE agents ran over fleeing man in
Texas, surveillance video shows. Judge orders Trump administration to pull
taxpayer-funded promotional ad. Justice Department opens antitrust probe of TV
networks over Trump pool blackout. Trump asks U.S. ambassador to Greece
Kimberly Guilfoyle to resign. Shawn Fain wins second term as United Auto
Workers president. Elon Musk pours $276 million into Republican midterm
effort. Pro-AI super PAC network routes millions through Nevada shell
companies._

_**International:** Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says Russia
violated Trump's "energy ceasefire," vows to respond if attacks continue. NATO
warns of counter-attack if alliance is attacked. At least 139 migrants dead,
84 missing after boat capsizes off Djibouti, UN's International Organization
for Migration says. China sanctions Paraguay's communications minister and
Belize's foreign minister over Taiwan ties. Dozens of gold miners killed in
airstrike near Sudan-Egypt border. Cuba denies connection to biodiesel
shipments seized in U.S. blockade. Spanish PM acknowledges Moroccan naval
incursion, calls it an "isolated" incident. Eritrea and Ethiopia trade
accusations of aggression, both appeal to UN for assistance. Gunmen kill at
least 20 in Nigeria convoy ambush. Rahul Gandhi leads march to India's Supreme
Court demanding election chief's resignation; 30,000+ police block the route.
North Korea test-fires multiple ballistic missiles, one flies over 900 km._

**This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday**

* * *

# Yemen

  * **Saudi-led coalition threatens Sana 'a oil site strikes; Ansarallah warns it will hit Aramco in retaliation:**

    * **Sana 'a:** Saudi-led coalition spokesperson Turki Al-Maliki announced plans for a "special operation" in the Ansarallah-held capital, and [issued](https://x.com/cjfcspox/status/2109983110402019342?s=46) a displacement order near the Yemen Petroleum Company's central Al-Sabaha station.

      * Any Saudi-led strikes on the capital would be met with a "harsh and painful response" in the Saudi capital, Riyadh, Ansarallah military spokesperson Yahya Saree [warned](https://x.com/yah_saree/status/2109980197013565630?s=46). Saree specifically [listed](http://t.me/army21ye) the retaliatory targets as: the Dammam headquarters of Aramco, the national petroleum and natural gas company of Saudi Arabia; Khalid Airport in Riyadh; and Aramco's refinery in Riyadh.

    * **Taiz:** Ansarallah attacks on Taiz reportedly killed five and wounded 17, according to the Yemeni Network for Rights and Freedoms. The attacks reportedly damaged several homes, Al-Safwa Hospital, and Al-Saeed Mosque. Yemen's Saudi-backed forces reported nine airstrikes targeting Ansarallah positions--five in Dhubab district and four in Al-Misrakh.

      * Shortages of medicine, fuel, and medical supplies threaten approximately 1,110 kidney failure patients and more than 190 intensive care patients, Taiz's local health office warned.

    * **Hodeidah:** Three airstrikes, including two on Kamaran Island and one in Al-Qanawis district were reported by Ansarallah-run Al Masirah TV, without immediate reports of casualties.

    * **Saada:** Saree claimed the group shot down a Saudi Wing Loong II armed reconnaissance drone while it was conducting "hostile missions."

  * **Riyadh airport still closed after Ansarallah attacks:** Operations are [still suspended](https://x.com/ksagaca/status/2109564392455250075?s=46) at Saudi Arabia's King Khalid International Airport following a series of Ansarallah attacks over the weekend that killed 14 people and injured at least 320. The closure was extended until October 17, affecting nearly 700 flights per day, according to Flightradar24.

    * On Saturday, an Ansarallah attack struck a passenger terminal, killing 13 and injuring 309, while a separate projectile hit Terminal 4 on Sunday, killing one and injuring 11 others.

    * Qatar Airways, Etihad, IndiGo, Air France-KLM, Lufthansa, and Air India have all cancelled flights to Riyadh. Cathay Pacific and Delta have postponed planned Riyadh services until 2027.

  * **Iran offers to mediate Saudi-Ansarallah talks:** Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi [offered](https://x.com/DropSiteNews/status/2109802713617756521) to broker talks between Saudi Arabia and Ansarallah, in a call Sunday with his Saudi counterpart, Prince Faisal bin Farhan.

    * Iran was ready to help start a dialogue and reach a political solution, Araghchi reportedly said. He warned that "insisting on a military approach and disregarding a political solution would only further complicate the situation."

    * Riyadh hasn't publicly responded to the offer. The Saudi Foreign Ministry said the two discussed "the recent escalation in the region and the efforts being made to address it," and that Araghchi initiated the call.

  * **Netanyahu is reportedly seeking Saudi approval to join war against Ansarallah; Riyadh opposes move:** Netanyahu is [seeking](https://x.com/DropSiteNews/status/2109806974057521485) Saudi approval, through U.S. mediation, for Israel to join the fight against Ansarallah, Haaretz reported, but Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman opposes the move.

    * The crown prince fears a domestic backlash if Israel enters the fight, according to Haaretz, while Netanyahu is hoping to strengthen ties with Riyadh and advance normalization. Saudi officials have said normalization depends on a path to a Palestinian state.

    * Last month, Lebanon's Al-Akhbar reported that he had offered "Israel's services" in a "comprehensive war" against Ansarallah.

# Palestine

  * **Israeli forces storm medical complex in Ramallah, raid prominent rights groups:** Israeli forces [raided](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/13/israeli-forces-raid-palestinian-ngos-and-hospital-in-occupied-west-bank) the offices of prominent Palestinian rights groups--the Addameer Prisoner Support and Human Rights Association and the Union of Palestinian Women's Committees--in central Ramallah on Tuesday, and stormed the courtyard of the Palestine Medical Complex.

    * Israeli forces confiscated equipment and files and arrested at least one employee from Addameer. Video obtained by Drop Site News shows the employee, who is seen on video being made to kneel outside the building with his hands behind his head in front of an Israeli army vehicle.

    * Troops stormed the Palestine Medical Complex, the largest government medical facility in the West Bank, deploying snipers at its entrances and preventing entry or exit.

    * Israeli forces [shot and critically wounded](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/10/13/%D9%85%D8%AD%D8%AF%D8%AB-%D8%A5%D8%B5%D8%A7%D8%A8%D8%AA%D8%A7%D9%86-%D8%A5%D8%AD%D8%AF%D8%A7%D9%87%D9%85%D8%A7-%D8%AE%D8%B7%D9%8A%D8%B1%D8%A9-%D9%88%D8%AD%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%AA-%D8%A7%D8%AE%D8%AA%D9%86%D8%A7%D9%82) a Palestinian man and injured a 14-year-old boy during the raids, and injured two journalists covering the raids.

  * **Israeli strike kills Palestinian in Gaza City as four-year-old dies of earlier injuries:** One Palestinian was killed and several others wounded Tuesday when an Israeli drone [struck](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/10/13/%D8%B4%D9%87%D9%8A%D8%AF-%D9%88%D9%85%D8%B5%D8%A7%D8%A8%D9%88%D9%86-%D8%AC%D8%B1%D8%A7%D8%A1-%D9%82%D8%B5%D9%81-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%AD%D8%AA%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%84-%D9%85%D8%B1%D9%83%D8%A8%D8%A9-%D9%81%D9%8A-%D8%AD%D9%8A) a vehicle in the Tuffah neighborhood, northeast of Gaza City, according to WAFA. Two Palestinians were also wounded by Israeli gunfire in the Al-Amal neighborhood and near Hamad City, north of Khan Younis.

    * Earlier Tuesday, a four-year-old Palestinian boy died of wounds sustained in an Israeli strike on Al-Zawayda in central Gaza nearly three weeks ago.

  * **Killed and wounded in Gaza:** Over the past 24 hours, six Palestinians were killed--three in new Israeli attacks and three due to wounds sustained in earlier attacks--and seven injured across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. One body was recovered from beneath the rubble.

    * The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 is now 74,389 killed, with 175,423 injured. Since October 11, 2025, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,498 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 5,306, while 838 bodies have been recovered.

  * **Israeli forces and settlers attack olive harvesters across the occupied West Bank:**

    * **Ramallah:** Dozens of Israeli settlers blocked Palestinians farmers from reaching their olive groves in Turmus Ayya, Ramallah, on Tuesday, WAFA reported, while settlers stole olives in Atara.

    * **Tulkarm:** Armed settlers [attacked](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/10/13/%D8%A5%D8%B5%D8%A7%D8%A8%D8%A9-%D8%B3%D9%8A%D8%AF%D8%AA%D9%8A%D9%86-%D9%81%D9%8A-%D8%A7%D8%B9%D8%AA%D8%AF%D8%A7%D8%A1-%D9%85%D8%B3%D8%AA%D8%B9%D9%85%D8%B1%D9%8A%D9%86-%D8%A3%D8%AB%D9%86%D8%A7%D8%A1-%D9%82%D8%B7%D9%81) olive harvesters in Beit Lid, beating and injuring two women, including an elderly woman struck in the head. Settlers also forced farmers from their olive groves in Wadi Al-Jameh and the Ramin plain at gunpoint.

    * **Nablus:** Settlers disguised in Israeli military uniforms [assaulted](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/10/13/%D9%85%D8%B3%D8%AA%D8%B9%D9%85%D8%B1%D9%88%D9%86-%D8%A7%D8%B1%D9%87%D8%A7%D8%A8%D9%8A%D9%88%D9%86-%D9%8A%D9%86%D8%AA%D8%AD%D9%84%D9%88%D9%86-%D8%B5%D9%81%D8%A9-%D8%AC%D9%86%D9%88%D8%AF-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%AD%D8%AA%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%84) a Palestinian family inside their home in Talfit, leaving several injured. In Beit Imrin, armed settlers forced olive harvesters from their land in the Al-Naqab area.

    * **Salfit:** Israeli forces [detained](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/10/13/%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%AD%D8%AA%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%84-%D9%8A%D8%B9%D8%AA%D9%82%D9%84-%D9%85%D8%B2%D8%A7%D8%B1%D8%B9%D8%A7-%D8%B4%D9%85%D8%A7%D9%84-%D8%B3%D9%84%D9%81%D9%8A%D8%AA-%D9%88%D9%85%D8%B3%D8%AA%D8%B9%D9%85%D8%B1%D9%88%D9%86) a farmer harvesting olives north of Salfit, fired tear gas toward other farmers, and forced them to leave.

    * **Hebron:** Settlers [assaulted](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/10/13/%D9%85%D8%B3%D8%AA%D8%B9%D9%85%D8%B1%D9%88%D9%86-%D9%8A%D8%B3%D8%B1%D9%82%D9%88%D9%86-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B2%D9%8A%D8%AA%D9%88%D9%86-%D9%88%D9%8A%D8%AD%D8%B7%D9%85%D9%88%D9%86-%D9%85%D8%B1%D9%83%D8%A8%D8%A9-%D9%85%D8%AF%D8%B1%D8%B3%D9%8A%D8%A9) olive harvesters in Masafer Yatta, stole crops, damaged farmland and fences, and smashed the windows of a vehicle transporting students to Al-Fakhit school.

      * Israeli forces demolished an agricultural room and water tank and uprooted fruit trees in Khirbet Soba. In Idhna, Israeli forces detained four journalists covering settler attacks on olive harvesters.

  * **Israel demolishes Palestinian homes inside of Israel a day after displacing 300 residents:** Israeli authorities [demolished](https://www.arab48.com/%D9%85%D8%AD%D9%84%D9%8A%D8%A7%D8%AA/%D8%A3%D8%AE%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%B1-%D9%85%D8%AD%D9%84%D9%8A%D8%A9/2026/10/13/%D9%87%D8%AF%D9%85-%D9%85%D9%86%D8%A7%D8%B2%D9%84-%D9%84%D8%B9%D8%A7%D8%A6%D9%84%D8%A9-%D8%A3%D8%A8%D9%88-%D9%82%D8%B1%D8%B4%D9%8A%D9%86-%D9%81%D9%8A-%D8%B1%D9%87%D8%B7) homes and agricultural structures made of metal sheeting in the southern part of Rahat in the Naqab on Tuesday, according to Arab48. The homes housed dozens of people. On Monday, Israeli authorities destroyed all homes in the village of Al-Dahiya, north of Rahat, displacing approximately 300 Palestinians of the Abu Wadi family.

  * **Netanyahu orders prosecution of soldiers interviewed in NAZA:** Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu has [ordered](https://www.theguardian.com/film/2026/oct/12/naza-netanyahu-orders-identification-prosecution-interviewees-documentary-film) the country's authorities to uncover the identities of the Israeli soldiers and officers interviewed in the documentary "NAZA" and prosecute them.

    * Netanyahu demanded the Israeli attorney general, the military chief of staff, and the head of Shin Bet "act urgently to uncover the identity of all those who are involved or appear in the libel film" and called for "the opening of a criminal investigation and prosecution."

    * The documentary by filmmakers Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor details Israel's mass killing of civilians in Gaza. Netanyahu has also said he would seek new laws allowing Israel to strip citizenship from people who "smear" Israeli soldiers as part of a campaign targeting Abraham and Szor.

# Iran

  * **Trump dismisses reports of Chinese and Russian assistance to Iran:** President Donald Trump said Monday he does not believe China or Russia are helping Iran in its war with the United States, dismissing reports they have provided intelligence and military assistance.

    * "If they are, it's at a very low level, but I don't believe they are at all," Trump [wrote](https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump/117431307261297275) on Truth Social. "They have too much to lose, and we would know about it, and know about it very fast!"

    * CNN [reported](https://edition.cnn.com/2026/09/25/politics/china-intelligence-iran-targeting-hormuz) that Chinese entities supplied satellite imagery of a U.S. base in Jordan before an Iranian attack that killed three American troops in July, as well as allegations that Russia shared intelligence on U.S. warships and aircraft. Moscow and Beijing have denied the reports.

    * At a campaign rally, Trump suggested the U.S. may have gone too far in targeting Iran's leadership, saying Washington is struggling to identify officials with whom to negotiate.

      * "We might have gone too far with the leaders because we don't know who the hell we're dealing with any more," Trump said at a campaign rally in Youngstown, Ohio. "Nobody wants to be the president of Iran," he claimed.

  * **IMF forecasts economic contraction in Middle East and Central Asia:** The International Monetary Fund (IMF) [projected](https://www.thenationalnews.com/business/economy/2026/10/13/imf-cuts-2026-growth-forecasts-for-gulf-economies-due-to-prolonged-hormuz-closure/) Tuesday that the Middle East and Central Asia economy will shrink by 0.3% in 2026, a sharp downgrade from the 1.9% growth forecast in April, citing prolonged disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

    * Kuwait is expected to suffer the steepest contraction at 16.7%, followed by Iraq (16%), Qatar (15.6%), Bahrain (11.3%), Iran (7.6%) and Saudi Arabia (3.3%).

    * The region is the only one globally projected to experience contraction this year; global GDP is forecast to expand by 3.1%.

  * **UK PM blames Iran for alleged plot targeting U.S.-used airbase:** A suspected plot targeting RAF Fairford, a British airbase used by the U.S. military in its war against Iran, was "almost certainly" directed by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), British Prime Minister Andy Burnham [said](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c6gr82ekqewyo) Monday.

    * The UK announced sanctions on two Iranian nationals over alleged "hostile activity," with Burnham pledging further measures.

    * Iran's Foreign Ministry [rejected](https://en.irna.ir/news/86291010/Iran-condemns-UK-s-baseless-claims-over-Fairford-air-base-incident) the allegations, calling them an "ugly conspiracy" aimed at advancing an anti-Iran campaign and deflecting responsibility for Britain's role in the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran. The ministry accused Britain of relying on vague language without presenting evidence.

  * **Attacks on ships near Strait of Hormuz reach highest intensity since war began:** Missile and drone attacks on shipping in and around the Strait of Hormuz [reached](https://www.ft.com/content/a4ab83d4-81b5-4336-9569-a0708b41e894?syn-25a6b1a6=1) their highest intensity since the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran began seven months ago, according to the Financial Times. Six vessels were attacked on Sunday alone, while 24 ships were hit in the two weeks ending October 11.

    * Oil shipments through Hormuz fell to just 2.9 million barrels on October 11, the lowest daily volume this month, according to Kpler.

    * The escalation comes amid increased Iranian attacks on vessels transiting through the southern route, as well as U.S. military operations to enforce its naval blockade of Iran.

    * On Saturday, a U.S. fighter jet disabled the cargo ship Ocean Molica in the Gulf of Oman for trying to break the U.S. naval blockade of Iran, CENTCOM said.

# Lebanon

  * **Israeli warplanes launch airstrikes across southern Lebanon despite ceasefire:** Israeli warplanes [struck](https://www.nna-leb.gov.lb/ar/news/568180/%D8%BA%D8%A7%D8%B1%D8%A9-%D8%B9%D9%84%D9%89-%D9%88%D8%A7%D8%AF%D9%8A-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B3%D9%84%D9%88%D9%82%D9%8A-5) in Wadi Al-Salouqi near the town of Shaqra in Bint Jbeil district on Tuesday, Lebanon's National News Agency reported.

    * Israeli forces carried out an airstrike on Kfar Tebnit in Nabatieh district, followed by another strike on Wadi Al-Hujeir in Marjayoun district.

  * **EU to establish mission to train Lebanese military and security forces:** More than ten European Union foreign ministers [agreed](https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/eu-establishes-new-lebanon-support-mission-2026-10-12/) Monday to establish a new mission in Lebanon to advise and train the Lebanese Armed Forces and Internal Security Forces, with an initial three-year mandate.

    * The EU is making an effort to strengthen Lebanese security forces and free up the army to focus on disarming Hezbollah, as part of the framework agreement signed between the Lebanese government and Israel.

  * **13-year-old killed, 24 wounded by unexploded munition:** A 13-year-old Israeli student was killed and 24 others wounded Monday when an unexploded cluster submunition [detonated](https://www.timesofisrael.com/student-killed-in-blast-near-lebanon-border-idd-as-9th-grader-elazar-yair-wilensky/) during a school hiking trip in the Ramim Ridge area of northern Israel, near the Lebanese border, The Times of Israel reported. Students had found the munition, authorities said, picking it up and potentially placing it in a bag before the explosion.

# U.S. News

  * **Ken Paxton celebrated New Year 's in Dubai with two indicted fugitives**: Texas Attorney General **Ken Paxton** , the Republican nominee for Senate, rang in 2025 on a Dubai balcony with girlfriend **Tracy Duhon** and two Americans who [left](https://www.wsj.com/politics/policy/ken-paxton-texas-senate-dubai-trip-b54292c3) the United States after being indicted on federal health care fraud charges, The Wall Street Journal reported on Monday.

    * **Anosh Ahmed** and **Sameer Suhail** are accused of embezzling $15 million from a Chicago hospital where Ahmed was the CFO; Ahmed is also implicated in a separate $195 million scheme involving fraudulent COVID-19 tests. He donated $190,000 to Paxton, including $25,000 days after his indictment. Both men have since returned to the U.S. to face charges.

    * Paxton also [received](https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2026/10/11/texas-gop-senate-candidate-ken-paxton-wrote-legal-opinions-that-benefited-large-donors/) campaign money from staff or political arms of five organizations with interests in matters his office weighed in on, the Washington Post reported.

    * Executives at slot-machine-style game maker Pace-O-Matic, for example, gave more than $100,000 while his office reviewed what counts as gambling. Texas Tech regents chair **Cody Campbell** gave $247,300 to Paxton's fundraising committee the day before Paxton threatened the Big 12 with a lawsuit over a disciplined Texas Tech player.

  * **Zohran Mamdani orders first NYPD use-of-force review in a decade** : New York City Mayor**Zohran Mamdani** [ordered](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/12/zohran-mamdani-orders-use-of-force-review-for-new-york-city-police) the first review of the New York Police Department's use of force in a decade, alongside reforms including $2.6 million in new funding for the Office of the Inspector General and a system to ensure disciplinary hearings finish before accused officers retire.

    * Reported use-of-force incidents tripled from 4,087 in 2016 to 12,348 in 2025 even as shootings and murders hit record lows.

    * Mamdani-endorsed congressional candidates **Claire Valdez** and **Darializa Avila Chevalier** have called for disbanding the department's Strategic Response Group. The group was controversially deployed at protests last week, following ICE's October 8 shooting of Oscar Belgal in Marble Hill. City Hall said the review was planned before the Marble Hill shooting.

  * **Federal agents raid Ilhan Omar 's D.C. home in immigration probe**: Homeland Security Investigations agents [searched](https://www.axios.com/2026/10/12/ilhan-omar-search-immigration) the Washington home of **Rep. Ilhan Omar** (D-Minn.) before dawn on Monday under a judge-signed warrant tied to an ongoing criminal investigation, the Justice Department said.

    * Omar is being targeted based on immigration paperwork filed in 1995 when Omar entered the United States as a 12-year-old refugee from Somalia in 1995. Omar became a U.S. citizen in 2000 when she was 17 years old.

    * President Donald Trump [told](https://www.washingtonsun.com/whitehouse/trump-raid-ilhan-omar-dc-washington-home-dhs-homeland-security-criminal-investigation) reporters he had "nothing to do with" the search, after weeks of attacks in which he urged her deportation.

    * Omar called the raid an attempt to "weaponize law enforcement" against political enemies, and House Democrats condemned the incursion as "deeply disturbing."

  * **ICE agents ran over fleeing man in Texas, surveillance video shows** : An unmarked SUV [carrying](https://abc7.com/story/ice-runs-man-agent-caught-surveillance-video-hitting-miguel-parra-hernandez-car-during-chase-shopping-center-harris-county-texas-officials-say/19930189/) ICE agents struck **Miguel Parra-Hernandez** in a west Harris County, Texas, shopping center parking lot on Saturday, as agents pursued another man they were trying to arrest, according to video footage obtained by the local ABC affiliate.

    * ICE claimed Parra-Hernandez ran in front of the vehicle, but the footage appears to show the SUV veering through empty parking spaces before hitting him. Parra-Hernandez was hospitalized and was reportedly in stable condition as of Sunday.

  * **Judge orders Trump administration to pull taxpayer-funded promotional ads** : U.S. District Judge **Jennifer Rochon** in New York on Sunday night [ordered](https://apnews.com/article/trump-tv-ads-f845554063cea0b4b41275d32abd3633) President Donald Trump's administration to cancel any remaining television ads paid for with $20 million in Department of Homeland Security funds. The ads, which began airing in late September, glorify Trump and echo his midterm messaging, with one touting the capture of Venezuelan leader **Nicol as Maduro**.

  * **Justice Department opens antitrust probe of TV networks over Trump pool blackout** : The Justice Department is [investigating](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/10/business/media/trump-justice-department-tv-networks.html) whether ABC, CBS, CNN, NBC and Fox News violated antitrust law when they jointly suspended pooled coverage of President Donald Trump last month after he barred CNN from the White House, sending the networks letters on Friday demanding communications about the pool and CNN's lost access, The New York Times reported.

  * **Trump asks Guilfoyle to resign:** The U.S. ambassador to Greece, Kimberly Guilfoyle, has been [asked](https://apnews.com/article/trump-ambassador-greece-guilfoyle-9da9d2e50e18bccc38946404c1ca756f) to resign from her post amid allegations of improper conduct, White House press secretary Katie Zacharia said Tuesday, according to the AP. President Donald Trump, who appointed Guilfoyle, [told](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/trump-says-hes-looking-at-firing-kimberly-guilfoyle/) reporters on Monday he is "looking at" firing her, saying "we're not happy," after businessman Eric Deters alleged she asked him to wire $100,000 to cover her American Express bill in exchange for help with the administration ahead of her 2025 Senate confirmation.

    * The Wall Street Journal, which broke the Deters story, also reported that Guilfoyle boasted in audio recordings about Greek businessmen paying for her travel and encouraged foreign governments to do business with one of them.

  * **Shawn Fain wins second term as United Auto Workers president** : United Auto Workers President **Shawn Fain** won reelection with 68% of the vote against five challengers, according to unofficial tallies, with his nearest rival, Vice President **Rich Boyer** , taking 14%; challenged ballots remain to be counted, and results are not yet certified.
